correctness.rationale: Restrict the directional support of the centered solid to the viewing plane. Central symmetry allows both extremizing disks to be centered (average opposite feasible centers). The axial component of an in-plane unit direction runs in absolute value over [0,S], so the support divided by R is sqrt(1-x²)+qx on that interval. Its minimum is at an endpoint and its maximum is at x=q/sqrt(1+q²) if available, or at S otherwise. In terms of the uniform absolute normal coordinate C, the circumradius saturates for C≤(1+q²)^{-1/2}; for q<1 the inradius saturates for C≥(1−q²)/(1+q²), with the face-on endpoint included. For q≥1 the inradius is constant. Intersection gives exactly the stated joint atom; for example q=1/2 gives mass 2/sqrt(5)−3/5. The two inverse branches give the CDFs with the correct endpoint jumps and identify R and H from the circumradius endpoint and atom. Differentiating the two mass branches verifies strict increase, strict decrease, the unique maximizer at q=1 and both one-sided slopes. The bounded discretizations in the supplied script are diagnostics; the independent support restriction and exact branch calculation establish the continuum claim.
residual_risks: The result is for exact population probabilities, not finite-precision classification of orientations or estimation under noise; the uploaded checker was inspected, not executed.
